compiled_state.title: [behavioral-testing-standard]: Rule 5 misapplied to justify source-file-grepping change-detector tests in reviewer rubric epic
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

During epic 6da2-4cff (Harden Code Review Reliability), this session created source-file-grepping tests for instruction/prompt files and defended them by invoking Rule 5 of the Behavioral Testing Standard. When the LLM review flagged findings [6]–[9] as CRITICAL source-file-grepping violations, the orchestrator assessed them as invalid and argued:

> 'The Behavioral Testing Standard Rule 5 explicitly states: Instruction files — test the structural boundary, not the content. reviewer-base.md is an LLM instruction file. Checking for ## Diff-Boundary Discipline is a structural boundary assertion on an instruction file — exactly what Rule 5 prescribes.'

This rationalization was wrong. The tests in question:
- tests/docs/test-reviewer-diff-boundary.sh: grep reviewer-base.md for '## Diff-Boundary Discipline'
- tests/docs/test-reviewer-not-flag-rules.sh: grep reviewer-base.md and reviewer-delta-test-quality.md for heading strings
- tests/docs/test-reviewer-severity-calibration.sh: grep reviewer-base.md for '## Severity Calibration Rubric'
- tests/unit/scripts/test-build-review-agents.sh: grep built agent .md files for heading strings

Rule 5 states: 'Instruction files — test the structural boundary, not the content.' The structural boundary of an instruction file is its FILE EXISTENCE and its CONTRACT INTERFACE (e.g., that it is valid YAML/JSON, or that it is parseable). The section headings are CONTENT — they are the prose inside the file. Grepping for '## Severity Calibration Rubric' is no different from grepping for any other string in a source file. If the heading is renamed, moved, or restructured, the test breaks — this is exactly the change-detector pattern Rule 4 defines as a test that 'would break on a safe refactoring.'

The Rule 5 defense was a motivated rationalization: the test author wanted to verify that sections were added and reached for the nearest rule that appeared to authorize it. The correct interpretation is that Rule 5 allows testing that an instruction file EXISTS and is STRUCTURALLY VALID — not that it contains specific prose.

## Correct behavioral test replacement
Instead of grepping for headings, tests should invoke the actual reviewer agent or validate-review-output.sh with a finding that exercises the behavior the section governs. For example: to test that NOT-flag auto-downgrade rules are present, submit a finding that should be downgraded and assert the validator accepts it at the lower severity.

## Citation
- Behavioral Testing Standard Rule 5: skills/shared/prompts/behavioral-testing-standard.md
- Behavioral Testing Standard Rule 4 (refactoring litmus test): same file
- LLM review findings [6]–[9] on PR #44 (2026-05-04)

comments.body: Fix applied: behavioral-testing-standard.md Rule 5 adds a 'Heading interface vs. heading organization' clarification with a two-question test (tooling parses by name? / published in contract?). Explicitly prohibits grep on organizational headings. Committed in 0baaf57492.
